$BTC Big week(s).

Either Bitcoin holds $80K throughout these next 1-2 weeks with: FOMC, Earnings, Election(s), IPO filing(s), End/Start of the month flows & whatever geopolitical headlines we're going to see.

In that case I think we go to $87K and take out those equal highs there and target $90K+.

If price does lose $80K we'll find ourselves in a solid high timeframe value area (I think) in the mid to low $70Ks. Might chop around there for a while and things will look scary. But from there I do believe we have a good chance of setting that higher timeframe higher low from the big impulse from $58K to the recent high at $87K.

Best to keep an eye on the headlines and see how the market reacts. That will be leading.

I think sentiment and outlook is pretty bearish already so if we were to absorb whatever selling happens down here and prices just start grinding up that'd be a big sign of strength to me and at that case I think this will just keep drifting up by shorts covering and sidelined/derisked capital moving back in over the days.

It's going to be very easy to get chopped up or shaken out of your bias in the next 1-2 weeks I think.

Easiest to just play things level by level and go from there. Don't assume supports or resistances break until you actually see it broken (on a daily candle close for example). That is how many people keep getting caught off guard.

Companies without strong, consistent revenue are finding it harder to rely on debt financing.

The bigger question is simple:

What happens if investors stop funding AI growth with cheap debt?

#Bitcoin – What’s Next?

The Big Sunday Report: All We Need to Know

TA / LCA / Psychological Breakdown

I have finished building the long positions I announced and entered between $80K and $81K. My average entry is now $80,400 for the longs, while my average spot entry is between 60-64k. Remember the sequence: My earlier predictions called a breakout above $82,500, followed by $88K, and it happened, and the time I made the prediction Bitcoin was trading at 60k. After the move into that target area, I prepared for the correction. At $88K, when everyone was calling for $100K, I was calling for $79K. Bitcoin did indeed crash to $80K, so I closed my entire short at $80,600, bought more Bitcoin spot and opened a long at that same price. I stopped waiting for the exact $79K target. The short served its purpose. It was a correction WITHIN a bull market, not my announcement of another bear market. To this day, BTC is still trading in the region I identified when it was at $88K. This tells me one thing: the $80K–$81K area, even extending down to $79K, is an accumulation zone. This can be observed clearly: spot demand is higher in this region, while long positions are also being built. If we analyse retail behaviour at this stage, we notice that MOST retail traders are extremely bearish. I will discuss this further below.

The $80K area is also a VERY IMPORTANT support level for bigger players, and this is something smaller retail players ignore. The average buying cost of Bitcoin for treasuries is at $80,200, with treasury and US spot ETF average entry buys are around $80K–$81.5K. It also reported that Binance spot bids around $80K had rebuilt by October 20 after the earlier correction from $88k. Meanwhile, realized profit-taking had slowed to roughly half its pace around the September high. Overall, this means the average entry of institutional investors sits around $80K–$81.5K, and profit-taking has slowed significantly. This tells me that the current selling pressure is coming from retail investors, combined with short positions in the futures market, while spot selling can be seen at the current prices from short term holders, but mid and long term holders do not dare to sell their BTC they bought at 60-70k. These conditions usually occur at local bottoms, and this is exactly why I am going long in the $80K–$81K region.

Now compare this with market sentiment. The Fear & Greed Index is at 54, but I question this reading because I see much more fear in the market right now. The reason is very simple: the Fear & Greed Index uses a calculation model, and most investors who purchased BTC in the last two to three months are currently sitting in profit. Those investors are experienced because they bought the bottom, they knew when to enter, its correct to call it smart money, while inexperienced investors have either not entered the market yet or are among those who sold in the last few days. So the Fear and Greed formula analyses 100% of the BTC owners behaviour, and sees that the 80% of experienced traders are holding and not scared. But if the Fear and Greed would be applied on the remaining 20% in the market, which are a massive minority, the fear and greed would be at extreme fear levels right now.

Now I explained you my points why I believe this is the bottom region, and I hope it makes sense. I keep holding my spot positions from 60-64k, and my longs from 80-81k and my target is the area of 94k. What I would love to see now is BTC reclaiming the EMA50 and close the daily above, and even if it does not, it becomes an indicator the bears can use and nothing else. I am confident that this is the local bottom

quote.text:
I've been digging into $PoUT for the last 3 days with Grok, checking the code, not just reading the posts. Here's what they've delivered.

Day by day, real commits. Their public GitHub has been updated almost daily. I cloned it and checked every update myself.

First check: 75 Rust tests passing, 23 of them brand new. Their Python reference implementation gave exactly the same results as the Rust code, and all 113 file checksums matched.

Their own review found bugs (storage accounting, validation logic), they fixed them publicly and added regression tests. Internal workspace went from 946 to 968 passing Rust tests with zero failures.

Today's commit: 52 files and over 69,000 new lines, including all 65,536 encoders (2^16) of a 4-bit test model, counterexamples, 128 deterministic request vectors and synthetic frames. I ran it: 52/52 Python tests pass, all 75 Rust tests still pass, and the checksums match for all 157 files.

Real tests, not cosmetic ones. Change a single value in the data and the tests fail immediately. Deliberately broken frames get rejected, and flipping even one bit gets caught. Everything runs offline and regenerates byte-for-byte identical, so anyone can verify it.

Honesty you rarely see. The dev openly says what's solved and what's still research, and doesn't pretend consensus is done. At this stage most devs post hype and roadmaps with zero code. Here you get commits, tests and checkable evidence, with the limitations kept visible.

A microcap with a working public repo, real tests and a dev who reports his own bugs is rare.

That's not hard proof, but it's a real link and it adds weight to the rumors.

DYOR, but I checked the code with Grok, and it holds up.

$BTC Loves following this pattern. During 2023-2025 we saw the same during the entire run up.

1. Volatility low, compression high, sentiment worsens
2. Sweep local lows (sometimes several times)
3. Retake previous low
4. Quick move towards top of range
5. Big move outside of range into new highs

Yet, during every consolidation, calls for a top happen and people willingly sell their coins. The easiest thing to not have this happen to you is to wait for candle closes and to see if a "break" below sees any follow through.

As you can see in these cases we had a few small breakdowns and price action below the initial support levels. Yet, there was never any considerable follow through lower. This means a lot of absorption is taking place.

Then when price recovers, sellers are mostly out and it flies with added short fuel too.

In today's case, $83K is a good first level for the daily closes to watch. From there, if bullish, you'd want to see quick acceleration to $87K+ without too much hesitation. Generally this takes less than a few days if the past 2 cases are of any indication.
